channel.title: Ofer Shapira
channel.description: Writing on AI agents, software architecture, and the systems that hold them together.

item.title: The Fully Agentic Company: The One Part No Agent Will Ever Run
item.description: Everything in an agentic organization can be substituted, the model, the CEO, every executor, except the one thing that authored why the work matters in the first place.

item.title: Context Snack fills the wait while AI agents work
item.description: I built a Cursor extension that serves relevant AI micro-news and retro games while your agent is busy.

item.title: How the Gauntlet Loop built a game from one prompt
item.description: Matt Shumer's Gauntlet Loop uses separate builder and critic agents to turn a broad Claude Opus 5 prompt into a Call of Duty-level game.

item.title: A four-step PR description for faster code reviews
item.description: As code output grows, review becomes the bottleneck. A structured PR description helps reviewers understand the flow and spot risks before reading the code.

item.title: Cursor’s SQLite swarm breaks human-speed workflows
item.description: AI agents rebuilt SQLite from its documentation and reached 1,000 commits per second, forcing Cursor to replace Git with its own version control system.

item.title: How agents choose among too many tools
item.description: Giving an agent more tools can make its decisions worse. Reducing the available options helps it choose more accurately.

item.title: Boris Cherny's AI adoption model fuels the bubble
item.description: A five-stage AI adoption model can reward token burn without accountability. Production agents still need supervision, and pretending otherwise fuels the bubble.

item.title: Turning feature development into marketing copy with Cursor
item.description: A Cursor agent in Slack reads commits, pull requests, and docs, then explains a finished feature to our marketing team in plain English.

item.title: Why we built a project just to throw it away
item.description: We built an entire system in two weeks, discarded the code, and used what we learned to design the production version.

item.title: An agent that tracks dependency changes
item.description: We built an agent that monitors the libraries and models our team depends on, then posts a weekly update in Slack.

item.title: What a 2026 résumé should look like
item.description: A PDF résumé feels outdated in 2026. I built an interactive version with Sticklight, including a scroll-based video background.

item.title: Detecting production bugs through missing Mixpanel events
item.description: Some production bugs create no errors at all. I added a daily Mixpanel scan that detects them by watching for missing events and unusual spikes.

item.title: AI changes the tools, not the engineering problems
item.description: AI memory and coding tools repeat problems software engineers have solved for decades. Strong engineering practices matter even more when AI speeds up development.

item.title: An agent turns every merge into a release update
item.description: I added an agent to our CI pipeline that explains every production merge in plain language and posts the update to Slack.

item.title: Why we ask AI before asking people
item.description: A quiet habit change is underway. People are turning to AI first because it often gives them a faster, more accurate answer.

item.title: How I use Rovo across Slack, Jira, and Confluence
item.description: Rovo searches company Slack and Jira history, then turns that context into Confluence documents for incident reviews and refactoring work.

item.title: Midjourney’s 60-second medical imaging machine
item.description: Midjourney Medical uses ultrasound to produce MRI-level images. It promises full-body scans in 60 seconds at one-tenth the cost of an MRI.

item.title: Using AI to analyze my team's pull requests
item.description: Cursor and Claude Code turn pull request history into a management and incident investigation tool.

item.title: How Google Stitch describes UI for AI agents
item.description: Google open-sourced Stitch’s approach to describing UI in Markdown, separating the visual layer from application logic so agents make fewer mistakes.

item.title: Cutting token costs in Cursor and Claude Code
item.description: Practical ways to control AI development costs by managing context, choosing models, delegating to cheaper agents, and monitoring usage.

item.title: Software engineering after manual coding
item.description: AI has turned code into an output rather than the goal. Software engineers now need to focus on architecture, critical thinking, debugging, and managing agents.

item.title: Mario's Cart shows how fast AI filmmaking is moving
item.description: A short film made with Seedance 2.0 shows how realistic AI video has become and how one person can now make work that once required a crew and a large budget.

item.title: Running a company on $400 a month with OpenClaw Agents
item.description: An OpenClaw Agents setup can cover research, content, video, development, and security for $400 a month.

item.title: A control tower for Cursor cloud agents
item.description: A keyboard-driven dashboard for running, tracking, and controlling 5+ Cursor cloud agents in parallel.

item.title: Qwen 3.5 brings a 397B model to local devices
item.description: Alibaba's Qwen 3.5 activates only 17 billion of its 397 billion parameters per token, making local AI processing possible without a cloud connection.

item.title: A 27KB pixel art office for Cursor's agent mode
item.description: I built a Cursor extension that turns agent activity into a pixel art office, using read-only JSONL transcripts and no image assets.

item.title: One prompt can now generate a complete short film
item.description: Generative video systems are moving beyond disconnected clips. They can turn a simple prompt into a coherent visual story.

item.title: World Monitor opens global intelligence to everyone
item.description: World Monitor combines live geopolitical data with local AI analysis in a free, open-source dashboard.

item.title: Building Hypes during a 42 km marathon
item.description: A runner built an entire app with voice commands during a marathon, using Wispr Flow inside Cursor.

item.title: Catching a $1,500 Cursor spend anomaly in real time
item.description: A developer spent $1,500 on Cursor in one day without anyone noticing. I built an open-source tool to catch usage anomalies and report them in Slack.

item.title: Portless gives local development readable URLs
item.description: Vercel’s Portless maps readable local addresses to the right ports, making local development easier for developers, automation, and AI agents.

item.title: A time machine game for practicing better reactions
item.description: I built an AI game that helps my 9-year-old revisit emotional moments and come up with a different response himself.

item.title: GitHub output from 10 prolific developers
item.description: I visualized public GitHub data from 10 developers, including their projects, stars, and the tools they created.

item.title: GitShow turns GitHub profiles into project portfolios
item.description: I built an open-source tool that adds npm download stats, project categories, stack visualizations, timelines, and sharing to GitHub profiles.

item.title: GitShow adds project context to GitHub profiles
item.description: Replace github.com with gitshow.dev to see npm downloads, grouped projects, tech stacks, focus areas, and a project timeline for any user or organization.

item.title: When extreme heat makes metal stronger
item.description: Northwestern University researchers found that under extreme conditions, heat can strengthen metal instead of softening it.

item.title: How OpenClaw became GitHub's fastest-growing project
item.description: Peter Steinberger built the first prototype in an hour, then kept it open source as it reached 180,000 stars and drew acquisition interest.

item.title: A Telegram bot that turns messages into calendar events
item.description: I built an open source Telegram bot that adds school events, birthdays, tasks, and appointments to my calendar from a simple message.

item.title: A real-world flight simulator built with Opus and Codex
item.description: The CEO of Grw AI built a flight simulator for real locations using Opus 4.6 for planning and GPT-5.3 in Codex for implementation.

item.title: Coding in parallel with Cursor
item.description: I run two coding tasks at once, catch up on Slack while they work, and let Cursor add the keyboard shortcuts it recommends.

item.title: AI products bring marginal costs back to software
item.description: AI products consume compute with every action. That changes software from a licensing business into a margin business.

item.title: Goose runs an open-source coding agent locally
item.description: Block's Goose offers a free, local coding agent that works with Claude, GPT-5, and open models through tools like Ollama.

item.title: Moltbook is a social network built for AI agents
item.description: More than 30,000 bots are already posting, replying, forming communities, and discussing how to communicate without humans.

item.title: Give Cursor access to your previous conversations
item.description: A User Rule can give Cursor access to conversation transcripts from the last 30 days, making them searchable and available for analysis.

item.title: Claude Code adds diff view for AI-generated code
item.description: Claude Code now lets developers review code changes and leave comments without switching apps, making AI-assisted development faster and easier to check.

item.title: How Cursor built my GCP browser extension in 30 minutes
item.description: A five-minute prompt gave Cursor enough context to research, build, and test a GCP browser extension using a technology I had never worked with.

item.title: Running multiple AI agents without terminal conflicts
item.description: Superset runs multiple CLI-based AI agents in isolated terminal sessions, making it easier to manage coding, debugging, and testing in parallel.

item.title: What one developer built with Google Earth
item.description: A single developer turned real map data into a live flight environment using open source code and existing infrastructure.

item.title: From Nokia keypads to AI intermediaries
item.description: In twenty years, communication moved from repeated Nokia keypresses and phone calls to low-friction messaging. AI may take the next step for us.

item.title: Kids will see hand-written code as ancient history
item.description: My 9-year-old built a memory game with Gemini, making me realize that writing code by hand has already started to look like a relic.
